sources.text:
Vättern ( VET-ərn, Swedish: [ˈvɛ̌tːɛɳ]) is the second-largest lake in Sweden, after Vänern, and the sixth-largest lake in Europe. It is a long, finger-shaped body of fresh water in south central Sweden, to the southeast of Vänern, pointing at the tip of Scandinavia. Vättern is a relatively deep lake, containing about half as much water as Vänern despite having only about a third of its surface area; its deepest point is 128 metres (420 ft) below the surface.
Vättern drains into Motala ström through Bråviken into the Baltic Sea, but since 1832 it has also had a downstream connection through the Göta Canal to Vänern and the Kattegat tributary of the Atlantic Ocean. The lake has plenty of sources from rivers and small lakes, with the highest located sources being near Nässjö on the South Swedish Highland near the southeastern shoreline.


== Name ==
The name Vättern is closely related to "vatten", the Swedish word for water, and also means "water, lake".


== Geography ==

stops.name: Vättern
stops.detail: Vättern ist nach Vänern der zweitgrößte See Schwedens und der sechstgrößte See Europas. Es ist ein langer, fingerförmiger Süßwasserkörper in Südmittelschweden, südöstlich von Vänern, der auf die Spitze Skandinaviens zeigt. Vättern ist ein relativ tiefer See, der etwa halb so viel Wasser enthält wie Vänern, obwohl er nur etwa ein Drittel seiner Oberfläche hat; sein tiefster Punkt liegt 128 Meter unter der Oberfläche.
